rows.source_location: PubMed abstract (Materials and methods, Results); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04419350 registry record (Design, Registered outcomes, Eligibility); no registry results posted
rows.diagnosis: ADJACENT: localized acquired hypomelanosis (registry: secondary to any insult, post-inflammatory or iatrogenic, larger than 3 cm); [not IGH]; whether any IGH was included is not in abstract
rows.design: randomized controlled trial; abstract says lesions randomized; registry says the area to be treated was split into two halves randomized by sealed envelope [within-lesion split, so the control half is not independent]; registry masking DOUBLE (investigator, outcomes assessor)
rows.body_site: not in abstract (registry eligibility allows any site except genitalia)
rows.analysis_unit: lesion (abstract: '80% of lesions' / '85%'; registry says each area was split into two halves, so [a 'lesion' in an arm may be a half-area])
rows.intervention: single session of microneedling, dermaroller 1.5-mm needles
rows.comparator: no treatment (untreated half of the same area, per registry)
rows.endpoint_definition: peripheral tanning (skin mapping of lesion surface area through transparent stencil paper, per registry)
rows.arm_result: median peripheral tanning observed in 80% of lesions
rows.patient_noticeability: not in abstract (patient satisfaction was a registered outcome; result not in abstract)
rows.texture_or_scar: not in abstract (scarring was a registered safety outcome; result not in abstract)
rows.uncertainty: Abstract wording 'Median peripheral tanning was observed in 80% of lesions' is ambiguous: it may be a median tanned fraction or the share of lesions with any tanning. Diagnosis: [not an IGH study; target is localized acquired hypomelanosis larger than 3 cm per registry, while IGH spots are typically small]. Abstract conclusion says 'localized acquired hypomelanosis in normal-texture and scarred skin', so the sample mixed scarred and normal-texture skin at baseline; results are not given separately. No between-arm statistics or p-values in abstract. Registry says each area was 'split into two halves then randomized', so [the control is the untreated half of the same area and spillover or a systemic effect cannot be separated]; [the untreated arm improved about as much as the treated arm]. Medians given without IQR or denominators. Registry says improvement was assessed monthly; only 3-month results are in the abstract. [Single session, so 3 months after start equals 3 months after the final treatment.]

verifier.notes: Verifier 2, 2026-11-27, judged from papers/excerpts/elhoshy2025.txt alone. Rows numbered from 0. No failed cells. Checked: every quote is in the source; arm_result matches the right arm and endpoint in all 10 rows (peripheral tanning 80%/85%, physician GAI 37.5%/33.33%, VESTA 37.5%/29%, patient GAI 50%/50%, surface tanning +3/+3 grades); time_from_last_treatment 3 months supported by 'a single session ... Three months later' and 'Time frame: 3 months post treatment', untreated arms marked not applicable; analysis_unit is 'lesion' only in rows 0-1 where the abstract says 'of lesions', and bracketed as inferred elsewhere; outcome_tier partial_repigmentation is the weakest reading for all rows (3-month follow-up, no complete or lasting match claimed); dark_overshoot, texture_or_scar, attrition marked 'not in abstract' correctly; uncertainty now covers the scarred/normal-texture mix (all rows), the unblinded GAI assessor (rows 2-3), the half-area split control, missing denominators and statistics. Minor, not failed: registry labels physician GAI 'mean' while the abstract reports a median; registry says intervention model PARALLEL although the area was split into halves.
